$comment: Spec for scripts/defence-mutation-record.mjs. Each entry removes ONE security defence and names the single test that must then fail. `find` must occur EXACTLY once in `source` — the runner errors out otherwise, so a refactor that moves a defence breaks this loudly instead of silently scoring it green.

the Redis tokenVersion bump used to run BARE inside the caller ambient tenant transaction (e.g. PUT /admin/users/:id) — a later COMMIT/audit-log failure rolled back Postgres while Redis kept the bumped version, a permanent lockout with no recovery path
being forgiven for a replay renews the refresh row's clock — a thirty-second window pays out a fresh twelve-month session

addItems opens a nested $transaction on a different connection from the ambient tenant tx, so cart_items.cart_id points at a cart the nested tx cannot see — P2003, a 500 on the first /cart/sync of a session, and tenantContext then rolls the cart back so the retry reproduces it

the bulk-sync loop loses its savepoint, so a same-line P2002 aborts a transaction the service does not own and every later statement throws 25P02 — the guard written to absorb the race surfaces it instead

defences.why: mergeGuestCart creates a second cart carrying the guest's own sessionId while the guest row is still live — a deterministic violation of the FULL unique index carts_store_id_session_id_key, which inside the ambient transaction aborts the whole request

a password reset stops bumping tokenVersion, so every access token already issued survives the reset for its full lifetime — the one action a compromised user performs, and the mid-flight guard becomes a no-op on that path

an exhausted grace budget is logged as an ordinary replay, so 'the cap is too low for how this merchant works' is indistinguishable from 'a stolen token was replayed' — and the cap being wrong is invisible exactly when it is burning someone's sessions

hop 1 of the successor walk becomes a per-user scan plus sort (there is no (userId, createdAt) index) instead of a primary-key read — a pessimisation on the thundering-herd path, where the chain is almost always one hop
the storefront allow-list is matched against the DECODED path only — `/stores/%70ublic/...` decodes into a permission and returns next() before the deny pattern is ever reached

/auth/refresh falls back into authLimiter's `<ip>-<email||unknown>` bucket — every refresh from an IP collapses into one counter shared with /mfa/verify, and a post-deploy herd 429s itself out of every session

the IP-only merchant-admin MCP rate limiter (the actual backstop behind the global-limiter bypass) used the raw req.ip, unlike every other custom keyGenerator in the repo — an IPv6 attacker rotating the low 64 bits of their address gets a fresh bucket per request, defeating the cap on this credential-stuffing surface

merchantMcpIpLimiterKey is the ONLY genuinely IP-only bucket on the merchant-admin MCP surface, and the global-rate-limit bypass for that path is justified entirely by this key being un-choosable by the caller — if it read the x-merchant-key header at all, a rotating/bogus key would fragment it back into unbounded per-request buckets, exactly the hole #1733 closed

merchantMcpLimiterKey used to key ONLY on the presented credential's hash when one was present, so the fingerprint sub-bucket carried no ip component at all — a real key presented from any ip landed in the same bucket, which is exactly backwards for the caller-cannot-choose-the-partition property the surrounding limiters depend on
the ADMIN single-post blog read (drafts included) is put back on the storefront allow-list, handing a merchant origin a credentialed cross-origin read of another tenant's unpublished posts
the THIRD frontend collapses a 429 back into a sign-out and wipes the only copy of its refresh token — an installed iOS PWA where localStorage is the sole store
the orders client re-swallows the throttle in its blanket catch, so the credential clear fires anyway

/auth/refresh falls back into the global 200/15min per-IP mutation counter it shares with every order and cart write, so a NAT'd office rate-limits its own sessions one layer above the per-user bucket

the merchant-admin MCP global-limit bypass matches req.path with a bare prefix, which also matches a traversal-shaped path like /api/v1/mcp/admin/x/../../auth/login — Node/Express do not resolve .. segments out of req.path, so a request literally targeting a DIFFERENT route could be exempted from the global mutation cap merely by prefixing it this way
a throttled refresh stops being retried, so the provider stays unauthenticated and the redirect effect routes the user to /login while their session is fine

the refresh bucket keys on an UNVERIFIED `sub`, so the caller chooses its own partition — a loop signing a fresh random subject mints a new 120/15min bucket per request and is never throttled, while the route sha256s and hits Neon before any signature check
the length ceiling before the HMAC is removed, so a 10mb body is verified once per request — the key generator becomes the amplifier the limiter exists to prevent

/verify-email falls back onto authLimiter's shared `<ip>-unknown` bucket, pooling every signup confirmation on this multi-tenant platform behind one IP with /reset-password, so one busy shared IP 429s other merchants' shoppers off a link that was never guessable in the first place

keying the verify-email bucket on the presented (unverified) token instead of IP lets an attacker mint an unlimited number of fresh buckets by varying the token string — the same bucket-shopping mistake an unverified jwt.decode makes for the refresh bucket

the mount-time session check stops retrying a persistent throttle beyond the single 1.5s inner retry, so isLoading goes false and the redirect effect routes an admin/staff user to /login within seconds of a throttle that would have cleared shortly after
same as mount-throttle-outer-ladder-not-abandoned-admin, on the orders PWA — the third frontend that must not diverge (Ruling P2-B2-5)

the admin mount check posts a credential-less /auth/refresh for every anonymous /login load again, draining the shared <ip>-refresh-anon and IP-wide refresh buckets the signed-in sessions behind the same office/carrier IP renew from (#2095, #2163)
same as admin-anon-mount-no-refresh, on the orders PWA — the third frontend that must not diverge (Ruling P2-B2-5)

/auth/me is folded back into the blanket /auth/ refresh-skip, so a customer's 401 on the storefront's own session check can never trigger a refresh — a signed-in customer with a perfectly valid refresh token is rendered a guest 30 minutes after login
merchant-supplied product imageUrl reaches fetch() unvalidated — the API host fetches cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 and Gemini describes it back to the merchant as alt text

every limiter is built at module load, before redis.connect(); a store that reads the client once at construction gets null and silently counts per process in production — per-replica budgets that reset on every deploy (#1862)

issueSessionFor mints a session for a suspended or deleted account; /auth/mfa/verify reaches it up to 5 minutes after login()'s status gate, so an account suspended mid-challenge gets a live session (#1864)
erasure deletes refresh rows but leaves tokenVersion, so every access token already issued keeps authenticating (warm tv cache) and an erased shopper can write PII back onto the row (#1871)
the bumped tokenVersion never reaches the tv cache the authenticate middleware reads first (key has no TTL), so the old access tokens stay valid despite the DB bump (#1871)
erasure stops reporting how many CRM rows it scrubbed, so a partial erasure is audited and shown as complete (#1880)

the platform-only origin gate stops refusing . / .. segments: the allow-list patterns constrain only the segments they name and the deny patterns match the UNRESOLVED path, so behind a proxy that resolves .. a merchant origin reaches /stores/:id/customers or /admin (#1820)
an inactive or soft-deleted store's custom domain stays a credentials:true CORS origin indefinitely (#1214)
a registered write tool that skips assertAgentWrite ships unauthenticated; the gate is per handler, so the registered-tool suite must catch a handler that forgets it (#1643)
the reset-email budget is keyed on the email alone, so flooding one store's account locks password recovery for the same address on every other store and the platform admin (#1861)
